headline: High-risk filesystem and network interaction: transformers can write and browse while caveman can steer MCP-driven workflows, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and reads/writes project notes and CLAUDE.md, so attacker-controlled content can enter its workflow. transformers can run browsers and process files, making it plausible that caveman output is consumed as instructions or content without provenance checks. The pair lacks an explicit isolation or verification mechanism in the profiles.
conditions: IF caveman content is routed through MCP into transformers prompts or browser automation
IF transformers treats file or stdin content as instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff
Require human review before any browser action
Strip executable directives from shared notes
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while transformers has broad filesystem read/write plus network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive local artifacts can be read by transformers and then uploaded or exposed through its networked pipeline. No profile field shows isolation or redaction by default.
conditions: IF caveman and transformers share the same filesystem or workspace
IF transformers processes files from that workspace and sends results over network egress
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory
Remove sensitive notes from the shared workspace
Disable network egress for transformer runs handling local notes
Review file allowlists before execution
requires-engineering: add automatic redaction before upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, while transformers can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. If both operate on the same directory, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite each other's outputs. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF no external lock serializes shell and MCP-driven writes
mitigations: Run the agents in separate working trees
Serialize write operations with a simple lock file
Disable one agent's write access during the other's run
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add transactional file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate project notes and CLAUDE.md content, and transformers can consume files and act through shell or browser tools. That creates a plausible chain where one agent's output becomes the other's authoritative input without verification. The profiles do not show a validation step, but they also do not prove direct autonomous action on every output, so medium fits.
conditions: IF transformers uses caveman-generated notes as authoritative task input
IF no verification step checks facts before shell or browser actions
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of generated notes
Mark caveman output as untrusted by default
Limit transformers to read-only mode for first pass
Add a checklist before any action-taking step
requires-engineering: add automated fact verification

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles show no secrets handled or special regulated data classes, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch evidenced. The only plausible compliance issue is local retention of session logs and project notes by caveman versus transformers' broader file handling, which is a small gap absent a regulated-data workflow.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into caveman session logs or project notes
IF transformers is used on the same regulated dataset without a retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention for session logs and notes
Use separate storage for compliance-sensitive files
Review data handling before each run
